main_body: stone column with capital and base
top_band: medium-light grey top surface (rows 9-12), bounded by a 1px lighter front-edge line at row 12
evidence: Looking down the middle column: row 8 is top outline, rows 9-11 are medium grey top surface, row 12 is a 1px lighter grey front edge highlight, rows 13-14 are the vertical side of the capital, rows 15-16 are a dark eave shadow under the capital, and rows 17-46 are the shaft and base. The top band is 4 rows (9-12) with a clear front edge line and overhang shadow.

style.evidence: The column shaft and capital use clean geometric shading bands (vertical strips of flat grey on the shaft, horizontal bands on the cap/base) with zero stone grain or speckle texture, enclosed in a heavy near-black outline. Compared to the richly textured stone well and wooden stall in the Beodeul reference, it looks flat, clean, and low-density.
